rv.q: Sharp performances from the cast, particularly by Glenister and Townsend, propel the story forwards at speed.

In fact, there are some moments in this enjoyably funny, often magnetic and occasionally lacerating evening when you miss the sheer ferocious passion of previous versions, but in general it does deliver the goods.

cn.t: Mamet's 1983 indictment of capitalism and toxic masculinity still thrills, elevated by a star-studded cast led by Christian Slater in a surprisingly humane production that interrogates greed and self-deception.
